title: Privilege Gateway: explainable RBAC core + runtime authorization middleware
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Build a single, explainable authorization "privilege gateway" that provides policy evaluation for API, runtime (inference), and console traffic. This ticket covers: 1) a compact, fast policy evaluator library with rich explanation traces; 2) sidecar/inline middleware adapters for API gateway, runtime frontends, and the Redwood Console; 3) audit event shaping and reliable sink plumbing; 4) SSO/SAML attribute mapping and session-scoped bindings; and 5) admin delegation primitives (grant/revoke via console + auditable approvals).
acceptance_criteria: Evaluator library exposes Evaluate(requestContext, resource, action) and returns decision: allow/deny + explanation trace <= 300 bytes
Middleware adapters for API, runtime, and console implemented and covered by integration tests (happy+deny+fallback+cache scenarios)

Audit events emitted for every decision with schema v2 (actor, action, resource, policy_ids, decision, trace_id) and delivered to both primary sink (kafka-audit-prod) and a fallback file sink on retry failures
SSO/SAML attribute transforms configurable via mapping rules in Console and honored by evaluator (e.g., group->role, email->principal)
Admin delegation UI flow implemented: can request elevated access for time-window; requests generate auditable tickets and enforce break-glass with MFA confirmation
Performance target: median evaluation latency < 350us in-process (no KV cache miss) and < 1.8ms for sidecar proxy path under 95th percentile
Graceful fallback: when evaluator unavailable, middleware must default to configured policy: fail-closed for admin routes, fail-open with audit for low-risk read-only routes
Security review completed and design doc signed off by security and SRE
Canary rollout plan validated in staging with synthetic requests, and feature-flag toggles present for per-tenant opt-in
technical_notes: Design choices: 1) Evaluator will be written in Rust and exposed via a small C ABI + Rust shim so it can be embedded in runtime frontends and compiled into sidecars. 2) Policy language: adopt a simplified CEL-derived DSL with explicit 'explain' hooks to produce compact reasoning traces suitable for logs and UI inspection. 3) Caching: two-tier cache — in-memory LRU for hot principal/resource pairs + distributed TTL cache for cross-process reuse. 4) Audit formatting: JSON Lines with deterministic field ordering, include policy_ids and truncated explanation (max 512 chars). 5) SSO/SAML: implement attribute translator module that can be hot-reloaded from Console-managed mappings. 6) Admin delegation: store temporary grants in Dynamo-style store with TTL and provide verification endpoint for middleware. 7) Telemetry: expose Prometheus metrics: eval_latency_seconds{path}, eval_denials_total, eval_cache_hit_total, eval_explain_size_bytes. 8) Backpressure: middleware should observe request queue depth and short-circuit with 429 when overloaded to preserve SLOs.
rollout_plan: Phase A: feature-flagged evaluator library in staging (unit+integration tests) -> Phase B: sidecar proxy enabled for non-admin API routes (canary 5% tenants) and monitor errors/latency -> Phase C: enable in-process evaluator in runtime frontends for cheaper hot-path inference (rollout by instance group) -> Phase D: enable Console enforcement and admin delegation UI -> Phase E: full default enforcement with fail-closed for admin endpoints. Rollback: flip feature flags and revert sidecar routing; audit events remain readable in the sink. Target production broad rollout by runtime-2.4 if metrics meet targets.
testing_plan: Unit tests for evaluator semantics and DSL parsing. Property tests for caching correctness. Integration tests that spin up a local sidecar + API gateway + evaluator and run thousands of synthetic authorize requests; assert decision fidelity and audit emission. Load test: run 10k req/s synthetic traffic against sidecar path to verify 95th latency and error budget. Security pen-test: run authz fuzzing to ensure no policy bypass. E2E: simulated SSO login flows with attribute mapping and session grants. Test artifacts: test matrix and harness in repo: github.com/redwood-inference/rbac-eval/actions (link below).
